messages:
Aisha Patel: oncall-bot just opened an incident for elevated SLO burn on /generation (burn_rate > 4x in 5m). link: https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-412
oncall-bot: INCIDENT INC-2026-412 detected at 1897654321 - service: api-generation - symptom: sustained 4.3x burn over 5m - paged: @oncall (priority P1)
Aisha Patel: paging me now. quick summary: customers saw degraded tail latency and some retries; most traffic fell back to smaller model but still heavy.
Rob Chen: seen it. logs show KV cache misses spike, and batching queue length doubled. suspect mis-routed traffic to a heavier model variant during a rollout.
Nora G: i see correlated deploys around 1897654200 for model-router service. @Rob can you confirm rollout ID?
Rob Chen: rollout id model-router/2026-03-15-12:42 (canary -> 30%). config change was a routing weight bump to variant-v2-quant.
Sam K: throwing up a quick dashboard: /dashboards/sre/model-routing-burn (live). added a panel for quantized latency breakdown.
Aisha Patel: mitigation plan: 1) rollback routing to pre-rollout weights 2) raise batching timeout to reduce queue thrash 3) mute noisy alerts for 5m while we stabilize. Can someone take rollback?
Rob Chen: rolling back now -> running: `kubectl set image deploy/model-router model-router=registry/redwood:model-router-20260314`
oncall-bot: DEPLOYMENT model-router rollback triggered by Rob Chen at 1897654390 - status: in_progress
Nora G: while rollback runs, i propose we adjust SLO burn alert windows so we don't page on transient spikes. current rule: burn_rate alert fires if 5m burn > 3x OR 1m burn > 5x. suggestion: require 2 windows: (5m > 3x) AND (1h > 1.5x) before paging.
Sam K: +1 to avoiding 1m-only pages; we should still surface to a channel but not page. can we implement as two-tier alerting? page when sustained across 2 windows, otherwise post to #eng-sre-informational.
Aisha Patel: agree. need to be careful: for true customer-impacting regressions we still want pages. maybe change paging criteria to: (burn_5m > 3x AND burn_1h > 1.25x) OR (error_rate > 0.5% AND burn_5m > 2x).
Rob Chen: drafting alert rule update now. here's the snippet i'll propose for paging rule:```yaml
alert: SLOBurn_Paging
expr: |
  (
    (burn_rate[5m] > 3)
    and
    (burn_rate[1h] > 1.25)
  )
  or
  (
    (error_rate[5m] > 0.005)
    and
    (burn_rate[5m] > 2)
  )
for: 3m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "SLO burn elevated and sustained for generation service"
```
Nora G: that looks reasonable. also add a non-paging noise rule: if burn_1m spikes > 5x post to #eng-sre-informational with auto-smoothing suggestions.
Aisha Patel: yes. Sam can you add a dashboard panel that shows the multi-window view side-by-side (1m/5m/1h) and the current rollout weights? that should help oncall decide quickly.
Sam K: will add panel and a toggle to overlay rollout tag. plan: create /dashboards/sre/rollout-burn-inspector. ETA 20m.
Rob Chen: deploy rollback completed at 1897654488. metrics trending back toward baseline; 5m burn down to 1.4x.
Aisha Patel: thanks. i'm going to mute the current noisy pager rule for 10m while we monitor. setting: `mute: SLOBurn_noisy_rule scope: generation service duration:10m reason: rollback in progress`
oncall-bot: ALERT_MUTED SLOBurn_noisy_rule by Aisha Patel - expires in 10m
Nora G: post-incident action items: - update paging rule as Rob proposed - add non-paging spike rule - add runbook step to check rollout weights before paging - include a checklist for model-router rollbacks in runbook
Aisha Patel: assigning items: Rob -> submit PR for alert change + test, Sam -> dashboard panels + share link, Nora -> update runbook, me -> follow-up with product on rollout gating.
Rob Chen: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/ops/merge_requests/2345 - includes unit test for multi-window logic.
Sam K: dashboard up: https://grafana.internal/d/rollout-burn-inspector - shared with eng-sre and eng-oncall.
Aisha Patel: good. couple follow-ups: 1) consider adding a soft quota circuit to prevent routing a flood to a single variant 2) schedule a short postmortem tomorrow 09:30 PT 3) measure customer latency impact (product) and add to postmortem.
Nora G: noted. i'll draft the postmortem skeleton and link the alerts/dashboards into it.
Rob Chen: quick note for alert tuning policy: we should standardize on requiring at least one medium window (5m) + a long window (1h) for pages on burn metrics, short spikes go to info channel. i'll add this to the SLO alerting playbook.
Aisha Patel: ok team, nice work on quick rollback. keep an eye for any regression, re-enable pager after the 10m mute if stable. :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT INC-2026-412 resolved at 1897654705 - root cause: routing weight change sent excessive traffic to quantized variant causing cache miss amplification - actions: rollback, alert tuning, dashboard added.
